newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Hindustan Times
BIHAR CHIEF MINISTER INTERROGATED

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) interrogated Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav in connection with the 10 billion rupee animal husbandry scam. An eight-member team of the investigating agency was led by its Joint Director U.N. Biswas. Details of the probe could not be known. The chief minister's interrogation was the last in CBI's agenda before preparing and submitting its progress report to Patna High Court on January 17.
The Economic Times
FIPB CLEARS TATA-SINGAPORE AIRLINES JOINT VENTURE

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has cleared the 24.8 billion rupee joint venture between Tata Industries and Singapore Airlines to set up a domestic airline. The FIPB will now refer the venture to the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment.
CONTROLLING STAKE FOR FOREIGN FIRMS IN AVIATION PROJECTS

The Civil Aviation Ministry recommended permitting foreign firms to take controlling stakes in infrastructure projects in the aviation sector. According to the draft policy, foreign companies would be permitted up to 74 percent stake in any venture dealing with aviation infrastructure, including airport projects. The draft policy also decided against permitting private domestic airlines from plying on international routes.
OIL MAJOR PLANS RISK PARTICIPATION

Indian Oil Corporation has introduced a new concept, risk participation, for banks in the $300-million foreign currency syndicated loan which is currently in the market. Bankers expect the deal would add a new dimension to the foreign exchange syndicated loan market for Indian corporates. The loan, which is being lead managed by Bank of America and State Bank of India, has given participating banks the option to either fund the loan or merely take on the risk.
The Times Of India
INADEQUATE PORT FACILITY MARS WHEAT IMPORT

Early last month the cabinet cleared a proposal for import of two million tonnes of wheat to curb the rising price of the commodity in the domestic market. Even before the cabinet clearance, official agencies contracted an import order of one million tonnes following verbal instructions to this effect. Sources, however, said the wheat might not arrive in time due to shipping problems. These official agencies had not contracted the entire remaining quantity after being informed that port facilities in India were not adequate for handling an import of two million tonnes, sources added.
Financial Express
TAKEOVER PANEL TO SUBMIT REPORT SOON

The long-awaited report of the committee on takeovers will be submitted to the stock market regulator soon. The first draft of the proposed code had been circulated for public opinion by the committee in August 1996. Changes were made in the original report following public reaction and feedback from the Finance Ministry. Sources said no major changes are expected from those already announced.
NEW AVIATION POLICY SET TO DASH HOPES OF PRIVATE AIRLINES

The new civil aviation policy would disallow foreign equity in domestic airlines and restrict the players from operating on international routes. Sources said the policy could be a major setback for private airlines. While ruling out the long pending demand of domestic airlines to operate on international routes in the neighbouring region, Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim, however, said the government had allowed the private sector to invest up to 74 percent equity in the area of airport infrastructure.
Business Line
MOVE TO MERGE ESSAR SHIPPING WITH SISCO

The Essar group has initiated moves to merge the two shipping companies in its fold -- Essar Shipping Ltd and South India Shipping Corporation Ltd (SISCO) -- and the boards of the two companies are expected to take a decision shortly. An independent valuer based in Madras has been appointed to work out the share swap ratio which will be finalised before the end of the month.
